full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts for disposal of the instant civil appeal, in brief, are that respondent Nos.1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.475 of 1985 before the learned Assistant Judge, Dacope Thana, Khulna [now Bagerhat] against the present appellants and respondent No.3 impleading them as the principal defendants stating, inter alit, that 17.23 acres of land appertained to CS Khatian No.124, corresponding to SA Khatian No.118 tinder Mouza Shabeherabad, Thana-Dacope, District-Khulna originally belonged to Biswanath Gain, Natabar Gain and Behari Gain to the extent of 4 anna share each and Jogendra Nath Gain and Mohendra Nath Gain to the extent of 2 anna share each. Biswanath Gain died leaving two sons, Joychand Gain and Balm Ram Gain, each inherited 2 anna share and they possessed the land amicably along with other co-sharers. Babu Ram Gain died leaving only widow Bhadra Bewa and two daughters named Alapi and Sarojini as his heirs and she inherited the share of her husband as life interest. She possessed land of her husband through bargader. Babu Ram Gain was a solvent person and he left no debt before his death. Bhadra Bewa was also solvent. But she transferred the suit land to the principal defendants at Taka 2,000 showing false plea of necessity of money by registered sale deed being No.1938 dated 12-7-1956. The said kabala was made without any legal necessity and it was not acted upon. The plaintiffs are sons of Pacharam Gain, who is the brother's son's sort of Babu Ram Gain, husband of Bhadra Bewa. After the death of Bhadra Bewa on 16-6-1983, the property of Babu Ram Gain devolved upon the plaintiffs as his reversioners. The plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by mutating their names in the relevant khatian. Since the impugned kabala dated 12-7-1959 was made without any legal necessity, the same is required to be set-aside as the plaintiffs being reversioners are in possession of the suit land. Hence, the suit for setting aside the sale deed being No.1938 dated 12-7-1956 and for confirmation of possession in the suit land. 

 16. Oral partition amongst sharers of 2[two] acres of land makes doubt in the claim of the plaintiffs. From a plain reading of the plaint, it appears that 17.23 acres of land appertaining to CS Khatian No.124 corresponding to SA Khatian No.118 under Shabeherabad, Dacope, Khulna originally belonged to Biswanath Gain, Natobar Gain and Behari Gain to the extent of 4 anna share each and Jogendra Nath Gain and Mohendra Nath Gain to the extent of 2. anna share each. Biswanath Gain died leaving behind two sons, Joychand Gain and Babu Ram Gain and each of them inherited 2 anna share and they possessed the land having amicable oral partition amongst the co-sharers. The pro-forma defendants are co-sharers and subsequent purchasers of the suit land. Babu Ram Gain during his peaceful possession of 2 anna share died leaving behind his wife named Bhadra Bewa as his only legal heir. Bhadra Bewa inherited the share of her husband as life interest. She was possessing the share of her husband through bargader. The plaintiffs earlier narrated that Joychand .Gain and Babu Rain Gain are the sons of Biswanath Gain and they inherited their father's share. In genealogical statements, it appears that Babu Ram Gain is the son of Biswanath Gain. There is no vivid narration of the plaintiffs' identity, so it creates doubt of plaintiffs' locus standi to file the suit. However, the reversioners cannot set-aside a deed of sale made by a Hindu widow of her husband's estate on the recited "ground that there was no necessity for such sale."
